section-head.purpose: Man-page .SH headings: NAME, SYNOPSIS, OPTIONS, etc.

term.purpose: All output in terminal blocks, white-space pre.

label.purpose: Terminal title bar and status chrome.

shadows.name: terminal-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: under terminal windows so output reads as a physical device.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: All state transitions (hover, reveal, color swaps).

motion.name: pager-slide
motion.purpose: The less-style pager reveal on scroll.

motion.name: typewriter
motion.purpose: Command explorer transcript reveal; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Options collapse to single column; pager drops its jump rail; copy button docks below the command.

components.name: Terminal Window
components.description: The tool speaking: dark block with chrome bar, LED, pre-formatted output.
components.css: .ds-term { background: #161616; border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); margin: 1.25rem 0; color: #d9d6cf; font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; } .ds-term__bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.85rem; background: #1e1e1e; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a2a2a; } .ds-led { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: #8f8b83; } .ds-led--on { background: #6fce8a; box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(111,206,138,0.8); } .ds-term__title { font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8f8b83; } .ds-term__body { margin: 0; padding: 1rem 1.1rem; font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.55; overflow-x: auto; } .ds-tp { color: #6fce8a; }

components.name: Copy Button
components.description: Micro uppercase hairline button; inverts to green on hover and on success.
components.css: .ds-copy { font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #d9d6cf; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #3a3a3a; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.35rem 0.7rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-copy:hover { border-color: #6fce8a; color: #6fce8a; } .ds-copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0e7a3c; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-copy:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Command Explorer Tab
components.description: Pressed command tab inverts to ink-on-paper; rest sits hairline-on-deep-paper.
components.css: .ds-cmd { font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.82rem; color: #1a1917; background: transparent; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid #d8d0c0; padding: 0.55rem 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-cmd:hover { background: #f5f1e8; } .ds-cmd[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #1a1917; color: #f5f1e8; } .ds-cmd:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0e7a3c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: The Pager
components.description: Fixed bottom less-style status bar: jump links left, scroll percent right, terminal-black chrome.
components.css: .ds-pager { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; background: #161616; color: #d9d6cf; font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; padding: 0.45rem 1rem; border-top: 1px solid #2a2a2a; } .ds-pager__left { color: #8f8b83; } .ds-pager__jump button { font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.78rem; color: #d9d6cf; background: none; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-pager__jump button:hover { color: #6fce8a; border-bottom-color: #6fce8a; } .ds-pager__pos { color: #8f8b83; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-left: auto; }

narrative.overview:
This site is not a website about a command-line tool; it is the tool's man page, typeset as a printed Unix manual. A homelabber landing on it should feel they have already opened `man tenda-n300` — the grammar of the manual (NAME, SYNOPSIS, OPTIONS, FILES, SEE ALSO, the double-rule header and footer) is the design. Where the manual talks about running the tool, the page becomes the tool: output is rendered as a real dark terminal block, not described.

The surface is warm paper with black ink, IBM Plex Mono throughout, and hairline rules. The only color is router-LED status: green for online/allowed, red for blocked/danger — used where live network state is shown, never as decoration. Density is high and steady, like a real manual page; the scroll is long, and the only interactive devices are a copy button, a command explorer, and a less-style pager that reveals on scroll.
keyCharacteristics: The whole page reads as one continuous man page, from header rule to footer rule.
Terminal output is dark blocks on warm paper — the only dark surfaces, and they mean 'the tool speaking.'
Mono type at every scale; hierarchy comes from weight and size, never a second family.
Status color is LED language: green and red only, and only on live output.

rules.name: The Two-LED Rule
rules.body: Green and red are the only chromatic colors on paper, they mean network status, and they never leave the terminal blocks. If a region is not showing the tool speaking, it is ink on paper.

rules.name: The Typewriter Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page leaves IBM Plex Mono. No display serif, no grotesque, no system sans. A second face anywhere is a broken promise of the manual.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper regions never cast shadows. Only a terminal block may lift, and only with the single documented shadow. A soft shadow anywhere else is decoration.

dos: Do keep every surface on warm paper with ink text unless it is a terminal block.
Do use green and red only to mean network state, and only inside terminal output (plus the focus ring and copy success).
Do render the tool's output as terminal blocks — author transcripts in the real format and label sample data as such.
Do set section heads as bold .SH-style manual heads; the man-page grammar is the identity.
Do reserve the lift shadow for terminal windows alone.
donts: Don't add a second typeface — the page is one mono family end to end.
Don't put status color on the paper or on chrome; LEDs live on dark terminal glass.
Don't use gradient text, glass, glyph icons, or emoji — iconography is the LED and the $ prompt.
Don't use cards, hero metrics, or kicker labels — the manual has no such scaffolds.
Don't let an em dash stand in for the man-page colon cadence; the manual speaks in colons and hyphens.
